record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Prove long-time existence in constant-mean-curvature slicing gauge for cosmological vacuum spacetimes with compact Cauchy surfaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g)$ be a globally hyperbolic vacuum spacetime of dimension $3+1$ (i.e., $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$) admitting a compact Cauchy surface $\Sigma_0$, and assume $(M,g)$ is cosmological in the sense that it possesses a Cauchy surface of constant mean curvature. A constant-mean-curvature (CMC) time function is a smooth function $\tau : M \to I \subset \mathbb{R}$ whose level sets $\Sigma_\tau = \tau^{-1}(\tau)$ are spacelike Cauchy hypersurfaces of constant mean curvature equal to $\tau$. In CMC slicing gauge, the Einstein vacuum equations reduce to a constrained evolution system for the induced metric and second fundamental form on $\Sigma_\tau$ together with lapse and shift determined by elliptic equations.

Prove that for every such cosmological vacuum spacetime $(M,g)$ with compact Cauchy surfaces, the maximal CMC time interval $I$ of existence is the entire range allowed by the topology of $\Sigma_0$; that is, establish long-time existence of the CMC-gauge Cauchy problem for vacuum Einstein equations with compact Cauchy data, showing in particular that the mean curvature $\tau$ exhausts $(-\infty, 0)$ in the expanding direction (or the appropriate maximal interval depending on the Yamabe type of $\Sigma_0$).
artifact.status_search_result: The long-time existence problem for CMC slicing in vacuum cosmological spacetimes with compact Cauchy surfaces remains a major open problem in mathematical relativity. Partial results are known under symmetry assumptions (e.g., U(1) symmetry, T^2 symmetry, surface symmetry) and for small perturbations of specific backgrounds, but the general conjecture has not been resolved. Related results address the existence of an initial CMC surface (Bartnik's conjecture), with both positive results under curvature assumptions and counterexamples (cosmological spacetimes without any CMC Cauchy surface) constructed for various spatial topologies.

status_evidence.title: Examples of cosmological spacetimes without CMC Cauchy surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Bartnik constructed a cosmological spacetime without a CMC Cauchy surface; more recent work enlarges the set of spatial topologies admitting such examples.
status_evidence.claim: The CMC-related existence questions for cosmological spacetimes are actively studied and not fully resolved; counterexamples exist for the related Bartnik CMC-existence conjecture.

status_evidence.title: A CMC existence result for expanding cosmological spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: If a cosmological spacetime satisfying the strong energy condition contains an expanding Cauchy surface and is future timelike geodesically complete, then it contains a CMC Cauchy surface.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial existence results for CMC structures in cosmological spacetimes are established.

status_evidence.title: Existence of CMC Cauchy surfaces and spacetime splitting
status_evidence.snippet: Studies existence of CMC Cauchy surfaces under curvature/completeness assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: General long-time CMC existence remains open; only conditional results known.
